cohort: 870 preterm infants hospitalized in a tertiary hospital over a three-year period
finding: The study observed a significant decrease in premature baby mortality rates over the three years, with the most common causes of death being respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, and pneumothorax, and mortality being significantly higher with lower gestational age and birth weight, and in those born via normal vaginal delivery and requiring oxygen immediately after birth.
mod_finding: Infants born via normal vaginal delivery had a significantly higher mortality rate than those born via cesarean section (p=0.010).
birth_weight: Mortality was found to be significantly higher as birth weight decreased (p<0.001).
